claim: Practising retrieval of some category members lowers later recall of unpractised members of the same category in human lab studies (RIF); direct replications give small effects, d about 0.3 to 0.4. Murayama 2014 pooled g=0.35 over k=512 samples (about 9 raw points; 4.5 to 5 when output interference is controlled).
agent_test: Quiz an agent on lesson A of a set, then test unpractised sibling lessons B,C vs lessons from an unpractised set, at equal tokens.

claim: Original RIF magnitudes are inflated: small samples (n=36, n=54) and no control of output interference. Meta-analytic g is 0.50 without control and 0.22 with control (Murayama 2014).
agent_test: Set sibling-damage thresholds at the replication size (about 4 to 8 points human), not original size.

claim: Restudy (re-reading) of the same items gives the same gain on practised items but no RIF in most studies; the retrieval act is what harms siblings. One 2022 paper shows restudy of the suppressed items removes RIF. Meta-analysis of 17 restudy samples: g=0.07 [-0.03,0.17].
agent_test: Compare in-context re-reading of a lesson vs a quiz on it; measure sibling accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Cue-independent RIF (strongest evidence for true inhibition) failed to replicate in the one direct attempt (d=-0.05, CI -0.36 to 0.27), but that result was uninformative, not a refutation.
agent_test: Use both cue-dependent and cue-independent probes of siblings in agent tests.

claim: Inhibition and strength-based competition (SAM) both explain RIF; the strength-independence correlation test cannot separate them; RIF without competitive retrieval was found by Raaijmakers and Jakab but a graded-shape study found retrieval-specific, strength-independent RIF.
agent_test: No theory choice needed: test siblings empirically.

claim: Context-change accounts compete: initial full retrieval shields siblings (small n), but a replication found context change alone does not cause forgetting.
agent_test: Before selectively exercising one lesson, run a full-set recall pass; compare sibling accuracy.

claim: RIF can be reduced or removed by manipulations: reward, restudy of suppressed items, integration of items, initial retrieval of the whole set, mPFC stimulation (RIF 6.25% vs 12.83%).
agent_test: After targeted practice, add a short restudy or integrate-siblings step; measure sibling recovery at equal tokens.

claim: RIF is larger with higher competition, low working memory capacity, high need for closure; it depends on executive resources.
agent_test: Vary demand for quick closure in the prompt and measure alternative retention.

claim: Evidence that RIF reflects one general inhibition process is weak: RIF, think/no-think and Stroop/Go-NoGo did not correlate (N=87).
agent_test: Low priority.

claim: The fMRI claim of targeted competitor suppression (Wimber 2015, N=24) did not survive a reanalysis and two behavioural replications.
agent_test: Do not rely on neural evidence for design.

claim: Retrieval practice can also help related items (retrieval-induced facilitation) when material is integrated and testing is delayed; about 4% (k=12 meta-analysis), about half the earlier 7 to 11%.
agent_test: Test whether linked lessons gain from sibling practice.

claim: Suppression (think/no-think) is a sibling mechanism; pooled effect g about 0.28 [0.14, 0.43] (search summary only).
agent_test: Check if an operator that drops a wrong idea lowers later access to its correct neighbours.

claim: RIF-like effect in LLMs: elaborating on one of several in-context items lowers later recall of the others (Qwen-2.5-7B -11.2 pp, 72B -24.9 pp); a one-turn list-all prompt restores recall (workshop abstract only). Numbers 11.2 pp (7B) and 24.9 pp (72B) now seen on the ICML page; still Qwen only, judge-scored, no replication.
agent_test: Replicate on our model: elaborate on one lesson, test the rest; then add a restate-all-lessons turn at equal tokens.

claim: Cue timing matters for the LLM fix: the same list after elaboration recovers 98%, before it -5% (72B).
agent_test: Place the full-lesson list after, not before, the targeted work; compare.

claim: In 39 LLMs, proactive interference (old values block new) is much worse than retroactive (d=1.73), opposite to humans; scale helps retroactive only (R2=0.491 vs 0.06). b23/b24/c18/c19 are the same paper; authors say it is not RIF.
agent_test: Keep newest-version lesson tagging; test stale-vs-new conflicts.

claim: Superseded memories keep being served: 70.3% of prompts expose a stale value without update resolution; keyed memory gives 92.9% vs 70.4% current-value completions.
agent_test: Slot-keyed lesson store with overwrite vs append-only; measure current-value answers.

claim: Models can say a belief is outdated yet answer from it when the question presupposes it (Premise Resistance 30% vs State Resolution 92% in one model); write-time adjudication (CUPMEM) gives 68.0% overall vs 5.1 to 17.8% for memory frameworks.
agent_test: Add keep/stale/replace labels at write time; test on lesson updates.

claim: Suppressing superseded memories at read time (same-slot only, query-conditioned) beats baselines; dropping forgetting costs 23 to 33 points; recency alone cannot tell competing from complementary facts. No ablation of labels and no false-stale rate reported.
agent_test: Implement same-slot-only suppression; check complementary lessons are not hidden (the RIF risk).

claim: A lossy compressed memory that keeps the conclusion but drops the source makes the model repeat the error; source-first memories reclaim after correction.
agent_test: Store source and conclusion together in lesson summaries; compare.

claim: Misleading post-event information lowers human memory accuracy: meta-analysis of 480 studies g=0.694 with very high heterogeneity (I2=92%); warnings after the misinformation reduce it; Loftus-Palmer wording effect.
agent_test: Insert a wrong hint in context; test whether a warning-after step cuts adoption.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: AI-written summaries with one wrong detail make people later recall the original event worse (83.6% vs 44.8% correct, N=328); AI vs human label made no difference; a chatbot with misleading questions tripled false memories (N=200).
agent_test: About human users, not agent design; informs summary quality.

claim: LLM summaries omit central details (51.6%) and 60% had at least one hallucinated addition, so summarising is a lossy, error-adding step.
agent_test: Measure detail loss of the agent lesson summaries vs source.

claim: LLM agents adopt false peer claims: GPT-5 error 17.63% to 41.59%, Qwen-235B 25.48% to 74.75%; long-term shifts far smaller for some models; prompt defences cut shift 46.0% to 17.8% (anchoring) or 26.5% (source scrutiny).
agent_test: State own prior answer, then test peer/context claims against it; compare shift rates.

claim: Embedding retrieval spaces reproduce human power-law forgetting (b=0.46) and DRM false alarms (0.583 vs 0.55) from neighbour competition alone.
agent_test: Check if many near-duplicate lessons reduce retrieval of each; vary neighbour density.

claim: Long-context drift starts after about 2,000 tokens in relational recovery, with lost and invented edges.
agent_test: Measure lesson-recall drift vs context length.

claim: Models stay consistent with their own earlier output (refusal inertia), hiding persuadability.
agent_test: Test with fresh vs retained history.

claim: Delay and sleep change RIF: related far pairmates were hurt without sleep and helped after sleep.
agent_test: Delay analogue unclear; low priority.

claim: Pooled human RIF (Murayama 2014, k=512 samples): g=0.35 [0.32,0.38], I2=63%; raw about 8.5 points overall, 10.9 uncontrolled, 4.5 controlled; fail-safe N 56,111.
agent_test: Use 0.2 to 0.35 sd, or about 5 points, as the expected human-scale sibling loss when sizing an agent test.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Output interference at the final test explains about half of RIF: g=0.50 uncontrolled vs 0.22 controlled (Q=77.0). Agent sibling tests need independent, item-specific probes, not free recall in one answer.
agent_test: Probe each sibling lesson separately, in random order, so the practised lesson cannot crowd the answer.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Integration of passages removes RIF in the one meta-analytic comparison: high integration g=0.01 vs low integration g=0.25 (k=7 each). Whether linking sibling lessons protects an agent is untested.
agent_test: Test sibling lessons stored as unlinked items vs one linked schema; probe after applying one.

claim: RIF is larger with strong competitors (g=0.51 vs 0.18, weak 0.00 once controlled), cued category recall (0.47 vs 0.27) and between-subject designs; after a delay it holds (0.40) once text materials are removed.
agent_test: Include strong and weak sibling lessons; expect more damage when siblings are close and cued by category.

claim: Wrong hints in memory or tool blocks are adopted: compliance 63% to 72% across five LLMs; success after complying 17% to 31%; placement (system prompt or footer) does not matter; showing memory only after a failed attempt is safer.
agent_test: Gate untrusted hints behind a first failed attempt; test whether source scrutiny beats this.

claim: In-context and memory-update interference is documented and prompt fixes are weak: latest-value accuracy falls as updates grow; telling the model to ignore earlier input has limited success; bounded memory costs 15 points (92% to 77%) on a frontier model.
agent_test: Same-slot supersession is the proven harm in stores; guard it first.

claim: No direct test exists of: RIF in a Claude-family or other frontier model, restudy vs apply for LLMs, retrieval from a memory store causing sibling loss, integration shields, a think/no-think analogue, collateral loss from write-time stale labels, or closure pressure on rejected alternatives. Only Li and Wang (Qwen) tested RIF directly.
agent_test: Run these as our own experiments; the claim set in the critique (gaps 1,2,3,4,6,7,9,10) is the test list.

claim: Premature commitment is common in frontier LLMs (53% to 82% false-action rates when the correct option is removed) and concision prompts shorten reasoning 12 to 17% with small, mixed accuracy changes. Neither measures loss of rejected alternatives.
agent_test: Do not claim that speed prompts erase alternatives; measure it first.
